# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 97 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 97 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_097_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 9, Chapter 14

**1** "All these," he said, "are glorious angels. The Lord is encircled by them. But the gate is the Son of God; he is the only entrance to the Lord. **2** No one shall enter in to the Lord except through him. Do not suppose that anyone can enter by any other way than through the Son." **3** I said, "I understand, Lord. But who are the six men who carried the stones?" **4** "These are the six holy angels of God who preside over all the virtues — the first things created by God; to these the Lord has entrusted the whole creation to increase and build it up. Through these six angels the tower is completed." **5** "And who are the others who are bringing the stones?" I asked. **6** "These also are holy angels of the Lord; but the six are set over them. When the building of the tower is completed, all of them together will feast in the presence of the Lord. **7** They will rejoice with the Lord over the completion of the tower." **8** I said, "Lord, I want to know what the stones represent." **9** "The square white stones that fit together perfectly — these are the apostles and bishops and teachers and deacons who walked in the holiness of God and governed and taught and ministered to the elect of God in purity and reverence. **10** Some of them have fallen asleep and some are still living. They always agreed with one another and were at peace; therefore their joints are exact — they fit the building of the tower perfectly."

---

### Translator's Note
The four-fold ministry of v. 9 (apostles, bishops, teachers, deacons) is historically significant as one of the earliest enumerations of Christian ecclesiastical offices. The emphasis on harmony and agreement as the reason for perfect structural fit is characteristic of Hermas's vision of the church as an organism of mutual peace. SOPHIA follows LOGOS throughout; PNEUMA's "no gaps between them" is evocative but paraphrastic.
